items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Jimmie Monroe, the husband of Nina Ma McKinney who was one of the movie stars who played in the first all negro movie called 'Halleluiah'.

ctx.x: But those guys were cats that were really ahead of their time. We all knew what's been going on for years in jazz since bop came on the scene. Now we play the melody in unison, written choruses and jive ones in unison and they sound good. But it just wasn't done in those days, except for this

group in Grand Rapids.
There was nothing outstanding about this group I was playing with. Zack played a not too bad banjo, Jimmie was alright on alto, Johnny Johnson played nice piano, the drummer was not too hot and I didn't raise too much hell on trumpet. Also I was not a critic. So we may not have been too bad as a group. I do know that we all enjoyed ourselves playing together and the public liked us, so maybe we were better than I could imagine we were.

At the end of the two months we came back to Cincinnati. I had decided before I left Grand Rapids that I was going to stay with my mother. My father and mother had separated for the last time ever since I was 14 years old. I and my brother had always been with my father and my sister had been with my mother all the time. I felt that I was old enough to do what I wanted to do, although I had a good father, I knew that I would always be like a young boy to him and not a young man.
